name: TANGO THERAPEUTICS

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That a $3.8bn market capitalisation for a company with zero revenue, a roughly $156M annual burn and a pivotal trial that has not yet started is self-evidently a price worth challenging, and that hiding behind 'clinical-stage assets are unmodellable' lets the most expensive name in today's ten pass without comment. The sharpest version adds that the market has just told me something: the stock fell 19.3% in five days on data the company chose to call 'promising' and chose to host a dedicated pancreatic-cancer webcast about. When a company stages a webcast for its best news and the stock falls a fifth, the informed reading of the data is probably worse than the adjective.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The actual response rates, durability and tolerability figures from the ESMO presentation set against the published benchmarks for front-line metastatic pancreatic cancer, plus whatever Revolution Medicines said about the same combination from its side of the partnership. Those would allow a probability to be attached to the pivotal study succeeding, which is the only input that matters.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The counter's observation about the tape is fair and I have recorded it as the market's own verdict rather than dismissing it. Where it fails is the remedy. I read the press release and the existence of the investor deck but did not extract the per-arm efficacy data from EX-99.2, and even with it I would have no defensible basis for converting Phase 1/2 response rates in a combination study into a probability of pivotal success and a peak-sales figure — that is specialist oncology judgment, not valuation arithmetic, and inventing a probability to multiply by an invented peak-sales number would be exactly the manufactured fair value this project forbids. The three numbers the brief offers are no help: an EV/sales multiple whose denominator is zero, a price-to-tangible-book that measures the cash being burned, and an unranked cohort. So the honest record is a refusal that explicitly declines to call the name cheap — on the face of it $3.8bn with no revenue is a demanding price, and a 19.3% five-day fall on the key data read-out is evidence worth carrying forward, not evidence I can price.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The efficacy and durability data themselves, which I did not extract from the ESMO investor presentation and which decide the name. Whether the first-half-2027 pivotal initiation holds. The company's cash runway in quarters — the Q2 release states management expects current cash, equivalents and marketable securities to fund the current operating plan but I did not capture the stated date, so I cannot say how close the next financing is. And the economics of the Revolution Medicines arrangement: a combination that depends on another company's molecule has value-sharing terms I did not read.

what_changed: The 2026-10-23 8-K under items 7.01 and 8.01, carrying both a press release (EX-99.1) and an investor presentation (EX-99.2), is the event behind the 19.3% five-day fall and it postdates everything in the model. Content: Phase 1/2 results for vopimetostat combined with Revolution Medicines' RAS(ON) inhibitors in MTAP-deleted and RAS-mutant metastatic PDAC and NSCLC, presented at ESMO, with an investor webcast focused on pancreatic cancer held the same morning, and a pivotal front-line MTAP-deleted pancreatic study guided to initiate in the first half of 2027. The second new fact, from the 2026-08-11 Q2 release, is financial and it changes how the brief's own multiples should be read: COLLABORATION REVENUE WAS $0 for the three months to 2026-06-30, against about $3M a year earlier, following the truncation of the prior collaboration. Net loss was $38M for the quarter and $78M for the half year, so the burn is running near $156M a year. There is no product revenue and now no collaboration revenue either. Earlier filings in the window — a 2026-06-10 item 1.01, 2026-06-23 and 2026-08-06 item 5.02 officer changes, and a 2026-06-08 item 7.01/8.01 — are not material to a valuation.
consensus_case: Tango Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company with no product revenue, and at $22.53 and a $3.8bn market capitalisation the market is pricing one hypothesis: that vopimetostat, its PRMT5 inhibitor, works in combination with Revolution Medicines' RAS(ON) inhibitors in MTAP-deleted, RAS-mutant cancers. On 2026-10-23 at the ESMO Congress in Madrid the company reported what it called promising Phase 1/2 results for that combination in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and non-small cell lung cancer, and said a pivotal study in front-line MTAP-deleted pancreatic cancer is expected to begin in the first half of 2027. MTAP deletion is a synthetic-lethal target with a genuinely large addressable population across pancreatic and lung cancer, pancreatic cancer has almost no effective front-line options, and a combination that pairs a first-in-class PRMT5 inhibitor with the RAS(ON) class — the most important new mechanism in oncology — is a credible way to build a franchise. The stock is up 189.2% over twelve months on that thesis. It is also down 19.3% over the last five days and 17.1% over 63, which is the market's own verdict on the ESMO data: the word used in the release was 'promising', and the tape read it as less than that.
base_case_rationale: No valuation is possible and none may be invented. The engine refuses on the cash flows, correctly: `nonpositive_normalized_fcff` and `negative_fcf_year_in_window` fire and base, enterprise value, FCFF yield and implied growth all print n/a for a company with no revenue and a roughly $156M annual loss. The multiples fallback has to be discarded as well, and on this name the reason is sharper than usual. The ev_sales row of 44.6x is computed on a trailing revenue figure that has already gone to ZERO — the denominator is the tail of a truncated collaboration agreement, not a product line — so it is not a sales multiple at all; this is the MARA defect in a different guise, where the revenue series does not describe the business. The p_tbv row of 3.7x is a measure of the remaining cash and marketable securities the company is consuming, so it mechanically rises as the balance sheet is spent. The two rows also straddle: ev_sales gives $6.75-$12.43, entirely below the $22.53 price, while p_tbv gives $11.56-$48.15, which brackets it — the RIOT condition. And the brief states the cohort is 'not ranked — too few comparable Health Care names'. What is actually being priced is the probability-weighted net present value of a clinical asset: the chance vopimetostat plus a RAS(ON) inhibitor succeeds in a pivotal trial starting in 2027, the addressable MTAP-deleted population, the economics of a partnered combination, and the dilution needed to get there. That is a decision-tree valuation this engine does not implement and whose inputs are not available to me from free sources.
key_risks: No product revenue and, since Q2 2026, no collaboration revenue either ($0 against about $3M a year earlier after the collaboration was truncated), against a net loss of $78M for the half year — roughly $156M a year of burn
